---
title: Theme CLI
description: Download and self-host Google Fonts with the puzzle-theme CLI, JSON configuration, subset selection, and cached build workflows.
---

The `@puzzle-ui/theme` package includes the `puzzle-theme` executable. Its
`fonts download` command fetches configured Google Fonts, saves WOFF2 files,
and generates a stylesheet for self-hosting. It runs during development or
your build, not in the browser.

With `fontSource="local"`, your application serves these files instead of
requesting fonts from Google at runtime. The download step still needs network
access to `fonts.googleapis.com` and `fonts.gstatic.com`.

For a complete walkthrough, follow [Set Up a Theme with Local Fonts](/docs/tutorials/theme).

## Installation and invocation

Install `@puzzle-ui/theme` using the [theme installation instructions](/docs/theme#install).
The CLI ships with that package; no separate CLI package or global installation
is needed. The package requires Node.js 20.19 or newer when using Node.

Run commands from your application's directory, where `puzzle-fonts.json` and
the public assets directory live. In a monorepo, this is usually the application
workspace rather than the repository root.

<PackageManagerTabs>
  <PackageManagerTab value="npm">

```bash
npm exec -- puzzle-theme fonts download
```

  </PackageManagerTab>
  <PackageManagerTab value="bun">

```bash
bunx puzzle-theme fonts download
```

  </PackageManagerTab>
  <PackageManagerTab value="pnpm">

```bash
pnpm exec puzzle-theme fonts download
```

  </PackageManagerTab>
  <PackageManagerTab value="yarn">

```bash
yarn exec puzzle-theme fonts download
```

  </PackageManagerTab>
</PackageManagerTabs>

These commands use the executable from the installed theme package. In a
package script, invoke `puzzle-theme` directly.

## Command and options

```text
puzzle-theme fonts download [options]
```

`fonts download` is the available command. The CLI does not create your theme,
write a configuration file, or update your React components.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config <path>` | `puzzle-fonts.json` | JSON file containing font roles. |
| `--out-dir <path>` | `public/fonts` | Filesystem directory for the stylesheet and WOFF2 files. Created recursively when needed. |
| `--subsets <names>` | `all` | Comma-separated Google Fonts subsets, such as `latin,latin-ext`. |
| `--force` | Off | Download again even if the existing generated assets are current. |
| `--help`, `-h` | Off | Print usage without reading configuration or downloading fonts. |

Relative configuration and output paths resolve from the current working
directory, not from the configuration file's directory. Value options also
accept `--config=./config/fonts.json` syntax. Running without arguments prints
help.

## Configuration file

Create a JSON object with at least one of the keys `heading`, `body`, or
`accent`. These keys match the [font roles](/docs/theme/typography#font-roles)
used by `Theme`. Do not wrap them in a `fonts` property or include theme tokens.

```json title="puzzle-fonts.json"
{
  "heading": {
    "family": "Sora",
    "weightRange": [300, 700],
    "display": "swap"
  },
  "body": {
    "family": "Inter",
    "weights": [400, 500, 700],
    "styles": ["normal", "italic"],
    "display": "swap"
  },
  "accent": {
    "family": "JetBrains Mono",
    "weights": [400],
    "fallback": ["monospace"]
  }
}
```

| Field | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `family` | Required | Google Fonts family name, including spaces, such as `JetBrains Mono`. |
| `weights` | `[400, 700]` | Non-empty array of integer weights between 1 and 1000. Choose weights supported by the family. |
| `weightRange` | Unset | Ascending pair such as `[300, 700]` for a variable font. Takes precedence over `weights`; the family must support the requested range. |
| `styles` | `["normal"]` | Requested styles: `normal`, `italic`, or both. |
| `display` | `"swap"` | `font-display`: `auto`, `block`, `swap`, `fallback`, or `optional`. |
| `fallback` | `["system-ui", "sans-serif"]` | Font-family fallbacks used by `Theme`; these are not downloaded. |

Use the role keys to assign fonts; a separate `role` field is unnecessary.
The CLI reads JSON, so comments, trailing commas, functions, and TypeScript
exports are not supported. Use exact Google Fonts names and supported
weights/styles; an unavailable combination can cause a Google Fonts request
to fail.

The JSON file can also supply the `fonts` prop when your application supports
JSON imports, keeping downloads and runtime family selection in sync.

## Subsets and custom paths

By default, the downloader keeps all subsets returned by Google Fonts for
each requested family. Limit this only when you know which writing systems
your content needs. `latin-ext` is separate from `latin`; include both if
you need both.

<PackageManagerTabs>
  <PackageManagerTab value="npm">

```bash
npm exec -- puzzle-theme fonts download --config ./config/fonts.json --out-dir public/assets/fonts --subsets latin,latin-ext --force
```

  </PackageManagerTab>
  <PackageManagerTab value="bun">

```bash
bunx puzzle-theme fonts download --config ./config/fonts.json --out-dir public/assets/fonts --subsets latin,latin-ext --force
```

  </PackageManagerTab>
  <PackageManagerTab value="pnpm">

```bash
pnpm exec puzzle-theme fonts download --config ./config/fonts.json --out-dir public/assets/fonts --subsets latin,latin-ext --force
```

  </PackageManagerTab>
  <PackageManagerTab value="yarn">

```bash
yarn exec puzzle-theme fonts download --config ./config/fonts.json --out-dir public/assets/fonts --subsets latin,latin-ext --force
```

  </PackageManagerTab>
</PackageManagerTabs>

Every requested subset must be present in the Google Fonts response for
every configured font, or the command fails. Subset names are lowercase,
optionally hyphenated, such as `latin-ext`. Omitting `--subsets` or passing
`--subsets all` keeps all returned subsets.

## Generated files and runtime setup

With the default output directory, the result has this shape:

```text
public/fonts/
  puzzle-fonts.css
  font-<url-hash>.woff2
  puzzle-font-<family>.woff2
```

- `puzzle-fonts.css` contains generated `@font-face` declarations with relative
  URLs to local files. Keep it alongside the generated WOFF2 files.
- `font-<url-hash>.woff2` files contain downloaded font resources. The number
  depends on families, weights, styles, and subsets; duplicate URLs are
  downloaded only once per run.
- `puzzle-font-<family>.woff2` files are stable preload copies, generated when
  a normal Latin face is available and the selected subsets include Latin.
  For Inter, the name is `puzzle-font-inter.woff2`. The corresponding CSS
  declaration uses that same URL.

Do not edit generated files. The CLI does not remove obsolete files from
previous configurations.

Downloading alone does not switch your application to local fonts. Pass the
same configuration to `Theme` and enable local loading:

```tsx
import { Theme } from "@puzzle-ui/theme";
import fonts from "./puzzle-fonts.json";

const App = () => (
  <Theme fonts={fonts} fontSource="local">
    <YourApp />
  </Theme>
);
```

`Theme` links `/fonts/puzzle-fonts.css` and preloads the body font by default.
Your framework must serve `public/fonts` at `/fonts`. There is no need to
import the generated CSS separately when using this setup.

`--out-dir` is a filesystem path; `fontBasePath` is the browser URL directory.
For `--out-dir public/assets/fonts`, use `fontBasePath="/assets/fonts"`.
Include any deployment base path in that URL when applicable.

Set `fontPreload="heading"` to prioritize the heading font, or
`fontPreload={false}` when no normal Latin face was generated for the selected
role. See [local fonts and preloading](/docs/theme/theme-provider#local-fonts-and-preloading).

## Caching and build integration

The generated CSS includes a hash of the resolved Google Fonts stylesheet
URLs and selected subsets. If that hash matches and all files referenced by
the CSS exist, the CLI prints `Google Fonts are already up to date.` and
skips network requests.

Changing the family, requested weights/range, styles, display, or subsets
invalidates the cache. Use `--force` to refresh unchanged configuration,
for example to pick up upstream font updates. This is a presence/configuration
check, not verification of the bytes of every existing file.

Add a script to your application's existing manifest:

```json title="package.json (scripts excerpt)"
{
  "scripts": {
    "fonts:download": "puzzle-theme fonts download --subsets latin,latin-ext"
  }
}
```

<PackageManagerTabs>
  <PackageManagerTab value="npm">

```bash
npm run fonts:download
```

  </PackageManagerTab>
  <PackageManagerTab value="bun">

```bash
bun run fonts:download
```

  </PackageManagerTab>
  <PackageManagerTab value="pnpm">

```bash
pnpm run fonts:download
```

  </PackageManagerTab>
  <PackageManagerTab value="yarn">

```bash
yarn run fonts:download
```

  </PackageManagerTab>
</PackageManagerTabs>

Run this before your development server or production build packages public
assets. Explicitly chain it into your build or CI rather than assuming every
package manager runs lifecycle hooks identically. Either commit the generated
assets or regenerate them during a network-enabled build; deployed browsers
need the generated files, not the CLI or configuration file.

## Errors and troubleshooting

Failures print an error and set exit code `1`. Treat a failed download as a
failed build step rather than deploying incomplete assets.

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Configuration cannot be read | Run from the application directory or pass an explicit `--config` path. |
| JSON parsing or role error | Use valid JSON with at least one supported role and a non-empty `family`. |
| Google Fonts HTTP error | Check network access, exact family name, and supported weight/style combinations. |
| Missing subset error | Choose subsets available for every configured family, or omit filtering. |
| Browser still requests Google Fonts | Set `fontSource="local"`; the default remains `"google"`. |
| Local stylesheet or preload returns 404 | Deploy the output directory, align `fontBasePath`, and disable preloading if no normal Latin face exists. |
| Fonts appear unchanged | Update the configuration used by both the CLI and `Theme`, rerun the download, and check browser/CDN caching. |
